t: To enable the Secretary to carry out the provisions of the National School Lunch Act (42 U. S. C. 1751–1760),$83,500,000: Provided, That no part of this appropriation shall be used for nonfood assistance under section 5 of said Act.

fable.w: This is a plain appropriation of funds for the National School Lunch Act, with a proviso barring their use for nonfood assistance. The tempting reading is that the school lunch program involves states and schools, but nothing in this text requires or authorizes consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It only makes money available and limits its use.
fable.s: To enable the Secretary to carry out the provisions of the National School Lunch Act

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation provision that allocates funds to the Secretary for carrying out the National School Lunch Act. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, nor does it create advisory bodies, public comment periods, or rights to sue. It merely restricts how the appropriated funds can be used.
qwen_block.s: To enable the Secretary to carry out the provisions of the National School Lunch Act (42 U. S. C. 1751–1760),$83,500,000: Provided, That no part of this appropriation shall be used for nonfood assistance under section 5 of said Act.

opus.w: This is a plain appropriation that funds the Secretary's administration of the National School Lunch Act and limits the use of the money. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. The Act's link to states and schools might suggest participation, but nothing in this section creates any process involving outsiders.
opus.s: To enable the Secretary to carry out the provisions of the National School Lunch Act (42 U. S. C. 1751–1760),$83,500,000: Provided, That no part of this appropriation shall be used for nonfood assistance under section 5 of said Act.
opus.b:
1. **Step 1 (reasoning):** One tempting reading is that the National School Lunch Act involves states and schools, so this section brings outside parties into the decision. That reading fails. This section only funds the Act's programs and limits how the money can be spent. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Any state involvement under the Act itself is not described here, and states receiving the money would count as benefit or grant applications anyway.
